name: Extremal index cluster switch
note: Ferro-Segers intervals estimator of the extremal index theta, computed from the inter-exceedance times of |r| above its own rolling 95th percentile, refreshed every re_n bars. theta is the extreme-value parameter for how much LARGE moves bunch, and 1/theta is the mean cluster size - a different quantity from GARCH persistence of the variance LEVEL. Low theta (extremes arrive in clusters) brackets the shock bar with a stop-buy at H+0.1 ATR and a stop-sell at L-0.1 ATR; high theta (extremes arrive singly) fades the shock into the prior close. Nothing is traded on non-exceedance bars or in the dead band between the two thresholds. Stated for daily bars; windows are expressed in bars because the study is intraday, and the estimator is scale-free. A bar where both bracket legs are touched claims neither, since the bar hides its own path.
source: Ferro & Segers (2003), 'Inference for clusters of extreme values', Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B 65(2) - the intervals estimator of the extremal index reproduced above. Leadbetter, Lindgren & Rootzen (1983), 'Extremes and Related Properties of Random Sequences and Processes' - the definition of the extremal index. Cited from knowledge; the web search budget was exhausted before I could open these, so verify the two-branch estimator formula against Ferro-Segers before implementation. The trading application is my synthesis.

def _theta_fs(pos):
    """Ferro-Segers intervals estimator of the extremal index.

    pos is the ascending list of exceedance bar indices S_1..S_N inside the
    window. The two-branch form is exactly as published: the (T-1)(T-2)
    branch is used whenever any inter-exceedance time exceeds 2, because the
    plain sum-of-squares branch is biased when clusters are widely separated.
    """
    N = len(pos)
    if N < 3:
        return None
    T = [pos[k + 1] - pos[k] for k in range(N - 1)]
    m = len(T)
    if max(T) <= 2:
        s1 = 0.0
        s2 = 0.0
        for t in T:
            s1 += t
            s2 += t * t
        if s2 <= 0.0:
            return None
        th = 2.0 * s1 * s1 / (m * s2)
    else:
        s1 = 0.0
        s2 = 0.0
        for t in T:
            s1 += t - 1.0
            s2 += (t - 1.0) * (t - 2.0)
        if s2 <= 0.0:
            return None
        th = 2.0 * s1 * s1 / (m * s2)
    if th <= 0.0:
        return 1e-6
    return 1.0 if th > 1.0 else th


def family_init(ctx):
    import math
    bars = ctx.bars
    n = len(bars)
    c = [float(b["c"]) for b in bars]

    r = [0.0] * n
    for t in range(1, n):
        a, b = c[t - 1], c[t]
        r[t] = math.log(b / a) if (a > 0.0 and b > 0.0) else 0.0
    ctx.r = r

    win = int(ctx.p.win)
    q = float(ctx.p.q)
    step = max(1, int(ctx.p.re_n))

    u = [None] * n            # the running |r| exceedance threshold
    th = [None] * n           # the running extremal index
    cu = None
    ct = None
    for t in range(n):
        if t >= win and (t % step == 0 or cu is None):
            w = [abs(x) for x in r[t - win + 1:t + 1]]
            w.sort()
            k = int(q * len(w))
            if k >= len(w):
                k = len(w) - 1
            cu = w[k]
            if cu <= 0.0:
                cu = None
                ct = None
            else:
                seg = r[t - win + 1:t + 1]
                pos = [j for j, x in enumerate(seg) if abs(x) > cu]
                ct = _theta_fs(pos)
        u[t] = cu
        th[t] = ct
    ctx.u = u
    ctx.th = th

    exc = [False] * n
    for t in range(n):
        if u[t] is not None and abs(r[t]) > u[t]:
            exc[t] = True
    ctx.exc = exc

    ctx.start = win + 2
    ctx._pmode = 0            # 1 = cluster breakout, -1 = isolated fade
    ctx._pref = None          # isolated mode's profit target: C before the shock


def signal(ctx, i):
    if i < ctx.start:
        return 0
    flat = not ctx.positions
    sig = 0
    mode = 0
    ref = None

    # ---- ISOLATED: theta near 1, this bar is a lone outlier -> fade it ----
    t = ctx.th[i]
    if ctx.exc[i] and t is not None and t >= float(ctx.p.th_iso):
        rr = ctx.r[i]
        if rr > 0.0:
            sig = -1
        elif rr < 0.0:
            sig = 1
        if sig:
            mode = -1
            ref = ctx.c[i - 1]        # the close before the shock bar

    # ---- CLUSTER: theta low, shocks bunch -> bracket the shock bar ----
    if sig == 0:
        a = ctx.a[i]
        if a is not None and a > 0.0:
            off = float(ctx.p.brk_atr) * a
            live = int(ctx.p.brk_bars)
            for k in range(1, live + 1):
                j = i - k
                if j < ctx.start:
                    break
                tj = ctx.th[j]
                if not ctx.exc[j] or tj is None or tj > float(ctx.p.th_clu):
                    continue
                hi = ctx.h[j] + off
                lo = ctx.l[j] - off
                up = ctx.h[i] >= hi
                dn = ctx.l[i] <= lo
                if up and dn:
                    break             # the bar hides its path: claim neither
                if up:
                    sig = 1
                    mode = 1
                    break
                if dn:
                    sig = -1
                    mode = 1
                    break

    if sig and flat:
        ctx._pmode = mode
        ctx._pref = ref
    return sig


def exit_signal(ctx, i):
    if not ctx.positions:
        return False
    held = i - min(p["entry_i"] for p in ctx.positions)
    if ctx._pmode < 0:
        if held >= int(ctx.p.iso_hold):
            return True
        ref = ctx._pref
        if ref is not None:
            px = ctx.c[i]
            if ctx._dir > 0:
                return px >= ref
            if ctx._dir < 0:
                return px <= ref
        return False
    if held >= int(ctx.p.clu_hold):
        return True
    return False
